The guide explains INTAKE from the human's side in '## Getting work IN: intake'. '### 1. Flag the item with a routing signal' shows the routing signal is a label (the concrete example warp-repo:web-app), with the component and named-field mechanisms named as the alternatives; for Confluence it directs the human to the shipped requirements template (plugin/templates/confluence-requirements-template.md) with its Outcomes, Acceptance Criteria, and Open Decisions sections. '### 2. Run intake' names the /warp:intake skill. '### 3. What you get back' states WARP drafts a routing-resolved warp.spec/v1 DRAFT bound to the resolved repo that the human then completes: for a bug the report becomes AC1 (the reproduction, written as a failing test) plus a no-regression ACn, for a requirements page the acceptance criteria come from the page (AC1..ACn) plus the no-regression criterion, with the source linked in intake_source. '### It refuses rather than guess' states intake FAILS CLOSED by name when the routing signal is missing, unknown, or ambiguous, never falling back to a default, so work is never silently misrouted.

Every piece the intake section names exists in the shipped engine: the routing mechanisms label|component|field and the fail-closed resolver are in .warp/tracker.py (MECHANISMS = ('label','component','field'); resolve_repo raises TrackerRoutingError on a missing, ambiguous, or unknown-repo signal); the /warp:intake skill is plugin/skills/intake/SKILL.md (a bug's first acceptance criterion is its reproduction written as a failing test, a no-regression ACn, the ticket linked); the intake logic that drafts a warp.spec/v1 bound to the resolved repo with intake_source and fails closed by name (IntakeError) is .warp/tracker_intake.py (draft_spec_from_item, draft_spec_from_requirements); the Confluence requirements template with Outcomes/Acceptance Criteria/Open Decisions is plugin/templates/confluence-requirements-template.md. selftest 1374/0 at e64b426 covers the tracker routing and intake suites.

The guide answers 'what happens to the ticket after, do I have to guess' in '## What happens to the ticket AFTER: the round-trip'. '### You do not hand-update the ticket' states the human does NOT hand-update it - a one-way MIRROR driven by the event stream (never polling) transitions the ticket's issue and posts a closing comment, with a table mapping the spec lifecycle to the ticket move (marked ready -> ready, blocked -> blocked, a review verdict recorded -> in_review, shipped -> shipped plus a closing comment, merged -> merged). '### Your own tracker statuses, via the status_map' shows a concrete small status_map and states an unmapped WARP status is recorded as a comment rather than an invented transition (omit the map -> comment-only). '### A plan builds an epic and children' states a plan's work graph mirrors onto an epic (keyed to the plan, never forked) and child issues. '### It is one-way, and the repository wins' states the mirror writes only status and comments, the repository is the single source of truth and wins any disagreement, it never polls, it is an idempotent reconciler, and an unwired spec is skipped by name.

The mirror facts match .warp/tracker_mirror.py exactly: EVENT_STATUS = {spec.ready:ready, spec.blocked:blocked, verdict.recorded:in_review, spec.shipped:shipped (+ closing comment), merge.completed:merged}; resolve_status_map merges the per-org status_map (global + optional per-repo) so the ticket uses the human's OWN statuses; an unmapped WARP status is a keyed comment not an invented transition (NG4); _epic_warp_status returns shipped only when every work item is shipped, else open; a spec with no tracker_repo, no config, or an unroutable repo is skipped by name. The one-way, repository-wins, never-poll properties are the tracker_status_mirror and tracker_epic_mirror capability entries in .warp/capabilities.yaml (reconciler, no processed-offset ledger, driven by the event stream not polling) and are consistent with the standing README rule that the repository wins if the index and any external tracker disagree. selftest 1374/0 at e64b426 covers the spec and epic mirror suites.

The guide's '## What "wired" means before you start' is actionable and true: it names the per-org .warp/trackers.json config (routing plus the status_map, template at plugin/templates/.warp/trackers.json), the optional tracker_repo front-matter field on a spec or plan (set for the human by intake from the routing signal, single-repository default when absent, fails closed against a wired config if it names an unknown repo), and auth by reference token_ref (for example env:JIRA_TOKEN, a secret reference resolved from a secrets store, never a raw credential in a config file, prompt, proof, or log, fails closed if none resolves), driven by plain non-LLM Python that runs unattended and deterministically. The mechanical-versus-reference honesty is preserved: the routing, mapping, intake, and mirror LOGIC is mechanical and gate-tested offline against an in-memory fake tracker, while the live Jira Cloud and Confluence Cloud connections are shipped REFERENCE implementations a repository wires to its own instance, and the round-trip is real once that live adapter is wired (do not assume a live instance is connected out of the box). No MCP claim appears anywhere in the guide - the connection is described only as non-LLM Python authed by a token reference.

Every module, config, field, secret reference, and template the guide names exists in the shipped engine: .warp/trackers.json template (plugin/templates/.warp/trackers.json, warp.tracker/v1); the tracker_repo field enforced parallel to the lane fields in .warp/validate.py (tracker_routing_enforcement, fails closed against a wired config on an unknown repo); the token_ref env: resolver and the fail-closed live adapters in .warp/tracker_intake.py; the Confluence requirements template at plugin/templates/confluence-requirements-template.md. The mechanical/reference split matches .warp/capabilities.yaml verbatim in intent: tracker_routing, tracker_routing_enforcement, tracker_adapter_seam, tracker_status_mirror, tracker_epic_mirror, tracker_intake, confluence_requirements_intake, tracker_conformance = mechanical (gate-tested against the FakeTracker); jira_cloud_intake_adapter, confluence_cloud_intake_adapter = reference (wired per repo, need a live instance, not run in the gate).
